fichas.title: Drainage and Rainwater Management
fichas.summary: Rainwater management aims to preserve the natural water cycle by avoiding or delaying runoff into sewers. Measures include soakaways, permeable paving, rainwater harvesting, roof planting, surface infiltration and rain gardens. Drainage may be linear or point-based; falls, inlets and collection routes should be designed to prevent water from reaching vulnerable structures or neighboring properties. Drainage installations can also be integrated into the landscape and paving design.
uses: Prevent water from draining toward buildings or neighboring properties

fichas.title: Rainwater Collection, Storage and Reuse Systems
fichas.summary: Illustrated systems collect roof runoff through gutters and downpipes, filter it, and store it in rainwater tanks or cisterns. Stored water can be used for garden watering or supplied to domestic non-drinking-water uses, with a separate drinking-water supply and system components such as overflow, pumps, valves, level indicators and running-dry protection. A drinking-water refilling system is cross-referenced to the rainwater system diagram.
